inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average count for FY2026 from the diluted-EPS note (Annual FY2025.txt line 11138: 29,952,094 thousand). Shares in issue at 31-Mar-2026 were 29,636m; the ~316m difference is unvested share awards and options. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count).
inputs.cash_composition: Cash and cash equivalents 3,573.632 + term deposits current 2,078.392 + term deposits non-current 3,458.412 (3.18% effective rate) + structured deposits at FVTPL 1,728.011 (bank wealth-management products, current, RMB4.4bn redeemed in-year). Restricted cash 36.369 excluded. Borrowings nil at 31-Mar-2026 (RMB396.7m repaid in FY2026). Lease liabilities (278.3) excluded under lease treatment B. ~RMB2.6bn of the pile is USD-denominated: CNY strength cost RMB227m of translation OCI in FY2026 and is an ongoing drag on the RMB value of the cash. Net working capital (receivables 5,303 + film/TV rights 2,991 + inventories 117 - payables 7,091 - contract liabilities 1,257) is ~RMB63m, i.e. the ticketing float owed to promoters is matched by receivables and content inventory, so the cash pile is not customer money in net terms.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest on bank deposits was RMB211.2m in FY2026 (finance income note 10; total finance income 258.5 includes a 47.4 FX gain). Under the Group's HKAS 7 policy 'Interest received' (109.2 cash) is classified in INVESTING activities and 'Finance income, net' (245.9) is deducted from PBT in the operating reconciliation (note 30a), so reported OCF and reported_fcf already exclude it. Set to 0 here to avoid stripping it twice; the deposits that earn it are in net cash at face. FV gains on structured deposits (38.2) and on listed/unlisted investments (16.1) are likewise excluded from the EBITDA margin anchor because their source assets are in cash / the equity bridge.
inputs.sbc_source: Annual FY2025.txt (year to 31-Mar-2026) note 30(a) cash-flow add-back 'Change in share-based compensation reserve' RMB75,559k, tying to the adjusted-EBITA reconciliation line 229 (75,559). Equity-award taxes: none disclosed (KPI EquityAwardTaxes = 0 every year). The RMB20.3m financing-activity 'Settlement of share-based compensation cost with ultimate parent' is the cash settlement of Alibaba-parent awards whose expense is already inside the 75.6 reserve movement, so it is not added on top.
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchases in FY2025 or FY2026 (last was RMB1.7m in FY2024); no dividend has ever been paid. The flat share count is a modelling convention the company funds only through issuance restraint, not through buybacks.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. fx_rate is HKD per CNY = 1.1722 (Yahoo CNYHKD=X, 2026-10-12), cross-checked against USDCNY 6.6915 / USDHKD 7.8469 = 1.1727 (0.04% tie). No dual listing exists for a parity check. Note the CNY has strengthened materially (HKD/CNY 0.853 vs ~0.92 a few years ago), which raises the HKD value of RMB-denominated IV and lowers the RMB value of the Group's USD cash.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular close, HKEX (last trading day before valuation date; daily bars carry normal volume, ticker is live not frozen)
inputs.latest_filing: Annual report for the year ended 31-Mar-2026 (file 1060.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt, labelled one fiscal year early), approved 27-May-2026. H1 FY2027 (six months to 30-Sep-2026) not yet published; no guidance is issued by this company.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~1.1 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~9.0% cost of equity; zero debt so WACC = CoE = 9.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios: content/regulatory/governance risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations rule f). House reference points: ~9% for JPY industrials, 10.5% USD tech default.
inputs.lease_treatment: B - leases as operating cost. Full FY2026 lease cash (principal + interest RMB36.2m, financing line 8360; 0.45% of revenue) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (232.8 non-current + 45.5 current) are excluded from total_debt; da_pct_path uses D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (PPE 57.7 + investment property 17.0 + intangibles 56.7 = 131.5, 1.64% of revenue; ROU depreciation 28.0 excluded so the lease is charged once).
inputs.nci_treatment: Bridge deduction at book (RMB252.5m at 31-Mar-2026). Flows are modelled on a consolidated basis; NCI took a RMB13.0m loss share in FY2026 so the book deduction is, if anything, generous to minorities.
inputs.ebitda_anchor: FY2026 operating profit 738.2 + SBC 75.6 + D&A incl. ROU 159.4 = 973.2 reported EBITDA pre-SBC; less one-off disposal/dilution gains (75.7 equity-method disposals + 26.5 deemed disposal + 4.6 dilution = 106.8) and investment-income FV gains whose assets are in the bridge/cash (38.2 structured deposits + 16.1 listed/unlisted = 54.3) = ~812 operating EBITDA pre-SBC, 10.1% of revenue. FY2025 on the same basis ~749 / 6,702 = 11.2% (after stripping the one-off RMB112m impairment reversal and FV items). Segment results (gross profit after allocated S&M) were 2,047 (25.5%): live entertainment 1,186 on 2,276 revenue (52%), IP merchandising 400 on 2,170 (18%), film 310 on 2,178 (14%), drama 151 on 1,401 (11%); admin expenses 1,502 (18.7%) absorb the rest. FY0 check: 812 - lease 36 - D&A 131.5 - SBC 75.6 = EBIT ~569; at 25% tax NOPAT ~427, plus after-tax deposit interest ~158 = ~585, against reported attributable profit of 705 that includes ~161 of pre-tax one-off gains and a 47 FX gain, less 28.5 share of associate losses - ties within non-operating noise.
inputs.fcf_anchor_note: FY2026 owner FCF of RMB2,411m is a working-capital windfall year: the operating reconciliation shows +1,837m of WC inflow (payables +1,484, contract liabilities +634, film/TV rights monetised +483, offset by receivables -615, inventories -114, restricted cash -35), after FY2025 consumed -1,917m building film rights. The 3-year average owner FCF FY2024-26 is RMB581m ((690.0 - 1,357.0 + 2,411.0)/3), which is the sensible anchor and is what the component build produces in year 1 (~RMB480m at a 10.3% EBITDA margin). The dashboard will show FCF falling ~80% from FY0 to Y1; that is the windfall washing out, not a forecast of decline.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md row 2: non-US operating company, with the adaptations file applied for currency, leases, NCI and the matching-asset rule). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY entry. Damai Entertainment (formerly Alibaba Pictures) is 53.56% owned by Alibaba Group; four segments: live-entertainment ticketing/content (Damai), IP merchandising (Alifish: Chiikawa, Sanrio, Pokemon licensing and retail), film content and technology (Tao Piao Piao, Yunzhi, film investment), and drama series production. It is an operating company, not a holdco, so the owner-FCF route applies - but the valuation is dominated by net cash (RMB10.8bn = RMB0.362/share = HK$0.424/share, ~95% of the market price), so the cash-at-face convention is the single biggest judgment: the company has never paid a dividend, is controlled, and the market is applying a controlled-company discount to the pile that the DCF does not. Each 10% haircut to net cash is worth ~HK$0.042/share. The share price fell 55% from HK$0.99 (Dec-2025) to HK$0.445 with no post-period event disclosed in the 27-May-2026 annual report ('no important event after March 31, 2026'); the cause is not visible in the filings and is described by the Analysis JSON as a de-rating with no disclosed event (sell-side targets cut from ~HK$1.3-1.6 to ~HK$0.9 while profits grew) - the bear weight is raised to 25% partly for that reason. Price is the 09-Oct-2026 regular close, not after-hours. Working-capital capture set to 0% in base because net operating working capital is ~zero on the balance sheet and the FY2025/FY2026 swings (-1.9bn/+1.8bn) are mean-reverting film-rights and payables cycles.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: segment build: live entertainment +10%, IP merchandising +25%, film flat, drama +10% weighted by FY2026 revenue mix = +11.4% year-1 base, decelerating to 3% by year 8
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 6.2% diverges >30% from revenue 3yr CAGR 31.6%. Revenue CAGRs are inflated by the consolidation of Damai (acquired from Alibaba for shares in H2 FY2024) and by the FY2026 drama-series ramp (+142%); equity CAGR is depressed by the FY2023 loss and FY2026 translation losses. Neither is a clean forward proxy, hence the segment build.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs are undefined: FY2021 (-RMB0.004) and FY2023 (-RMB0.011) were losses. Owner-FCF CAGRs (reported FCF less SBC; interest already outside OCF under HKAS 7 classification, all years) run FY2023 423.3 -> FY2026 2,411.0 and FY2021 100.5 -> FY2026 2,411.0 and are meaningless as trend indicators because both endpoints are working-capital driven (owner FCF: FY19 -1,490, FY20 -905, FY21 +101, FY22 -661, FY23 +423, FY24 +690, FY25 -1,357, FY26 +2,411). Owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported-FCF CAGR because SBC fell from RMB147m (FY2023) to RMB76m (FY2026), the opposite of the SBC-outgrowing-cash warning.

base.growth_rationale: Live entertainment +10% (industry box office +6%, Damai gaining share; 400k+ shows ticketed, on-site events +50%), IP merchandising +25% decelerating from +60% as Chiikawa/Sanrio retail store roll-out continues but the FY2026 base is already large, film flat after -20% ('cold winter', deliberately smaller slate), drama +10% off a lumpy +142% year. Blended +11%, fading to China nominal-GDP-like 3%.
base.margin_rationale: 10.3% in Y1 is a half-point recovery from FY2026's 10.1% (which absorbed innovation-business share-buying in live entertainment and IP sub-line shutdown losses), ramping to 13% as the 52%-gross-margin ticketing business and Alifish scale over an admin base growing slower than revenue. Capped at 13% because film and drama (11-14% segment margins) remain ~45% of revenue.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 cash tax 149m / pre-interest pre-one-off EBIT ~569m = 26%; current tax expense 185m; PRC statutory 25% with HK/high-tech subsidiaries at lower rates offset by unrecognised losses. Start at 22% (remaining RMB123m deferred tax assets, loss utilisation) and ramp to 25% statutory by Y4.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex 163.4 (2.0%: PPE 161.6 + intangibles 1.8) and FY2025 176.4 (2.6%) as venue/office PPE built; converging to D&A (1.5%) once the build-out matures.
base.terminal_rationale: 15x cap (not the 20x US-compounder default) for an HK-listed China content/ticketing group with a cyclical film arm; 2.5% terminal growth in RMB.

bull.narrative: IP merchandising sustains +30-40% for two more years on flagship-store replication and Tmall pop-toy co-operation; Maiseat (SE Asia/Korea ticketing) and overseas Mandarin tours make international a real segment; live-entertainment margin recovers to 55% as innovation spend matures; drama pipeline (20+ projects) monetises. Ticketing float and contract liabilities grow with GMV (5% capture of revenue growth). No cash returned, but no value-destroying deployment either.

bear.narrative: Regulators cap concert ticket pricing / mandate refund terms and squeeze Damai's take rate while the post-COVID concert boom normalises (industry box office growth already slowed to +6%); the Chiikawa/pop-toy cycle fades and IP merchandising stalls; the film arm returns to losses in a weak box office; drama working capital consumes cash. Capex held at 3% of revenue to represent content and venue investment that earns no return (the Alibaba-ecosystem capital-allocation risk), and 5% of revenue growth absorbed by working capital. Net cash is still credited at face - the bear value is therefore a floor only if the cash is not deployed into related-party or loss-making content.

scenario_narratives.base: Damai remains China's leading live-entertainment ticketing platform, growing a few points faster than a +6% industry while its gross margin stabilises around 50%; Alifish IP merchandising keeps compounding at 25% then decelerates as the flagship-store model matures; film is run as a small, low-risk slate and drama grows modestly off a lumpy year. Group revenue grows 11% in FY2027 fading to 3% by FY2034; operating EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, ex one-offs) rises from 10.1% to 13% on admin leverage; cash tax ramps 22% to 25%; capex converges to D&A. The RMB10.8bn net cash pile (zero borrowings) is credited at face but earns nothing inside the flows. FY2026's RMB2.4bn owner FCF is treated as a working-capital windfall; the model's year-1 owner FCF is ~RMB480m, in line with the FY2024-26 average of RMB581m.
scenario_narratives.bull: IP merchandising and international (Maiseat, overseas tours) become second and third growth engines alongside ticketing; margins reach 15.5% by year 9; the ticketing float grows with GMV. Revenue roughly doubles over ten years.
scenario_narratives.bear: Ticketing take-rate regulation and concert-market normalisation flatten revenue for three years; the pop-toy IP cycle fades; film returns to losses; margins compress to 7.5%; capital is deployed at 3% of revenue into content and venues with no return and working capital absorbs cash. Net cash still provides most of the value - the risk the model cannot price is that the cash itself is spent badly or never returned.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: single-regulator exposure (PRC culture/market regulators on ticketing pricing and refunds), a 53.6% controlling shareholder with a history of related-party transactions and no dividend ever paid against a cash pile worth ~95% of the market cap, and an unexplained 55% share-price fall since Dec-2025 that the filings do not account for. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs IP merchandising, international and content margins all to deliver independently, and this company's film arm has a decade of losses behind it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on the consolidated operating business plus net cash and bridge assets at (haircut) book. At the current price the market capitalisation (~HK$13.3bn, ~RMB11.4bn) is roughly equal to net cash (RMB10.8bn) plus bridge assets (RMB0.6bn): the operating business - RMB2bn of segment profit, ~RMB570m of EBIT, the leading ticketing platform in China - is being priced at approximately zero. The DCF credits the cash at face, which is correct for an owner who controls it; a minority holder in a 53.6% Alibaba-controlled company that has never paid a dividend does not, and the gap between the DCF and the price is mostly the market's discount on that pile. Read the bear case as the floor only if the cash is preserved.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net cash is ~95% of the market price and is credited at face: every 10% haircut (controlled-company discount, trapped cash, poor deployment) is worth ~HK$0.042/share.

Distribution and payments dependency on Alibaba platforms (Alipay, Taobao/Tmall) under continuing connected-transaction agreements: a change in intra-group terms or de-prioritisation would hit user acquisition and take rate directly (Analysis JSON: high severity).

Controlling shareholder (Alibaba 53.56%) with extensive connected transactions (Tmall, Alipay, Youku, parent SBC settlements); capital allocation into film/drama content has destroyed value in FY2019-2023 (cumulative losses ~RMB3.5bn).
Regulatory: PRC rules on concert ticket pricing, real-name ticketing and refunds can compress Damai's take rate; film censorship and release windows.
Working-capital volatility: FY2025 -RMB1.9bn / FY2026 +RMB1.8bn swings from film-rights investment and promoter payables; reported FCF is not a readable annual signal.
FX: ~RMB2.6bn of cash is USD-denominated; continued CNY appreciation reduces its RMB value (RMB227m translation loss in FY2026).
Share-price collapse from HK$0.99 (Dec-2025) to HK$0.445 is unexplained by the 27-May-2026 annual report; H1 FY2027 results (due Nov-2026) are the next evidence.
IP merchandising (+60% in FY2026) rides a Chiikawa/pop-toy cycle that may not persist; drama (+142%) is project-lumpy.
